newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurds mark deaths in Halabja gas attacks.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurds mark deaths in Halabja gas attacks.

text.p: Kurds in northern Iraq were to observe a minute's silence on Sunday to mark the anniversary of an Iraqi government gas attack that killed an estimated 5,000 people in the town of Halabja in 1988.

"It is a tradition now in every town and village to hold a minute's silence to remember those who died and to discuss again the latest situation in the Kurdish question," Kurdish Democratic Party (KDP) Ankara spokesman Faik Nerweyi told Reuters.
"The people will be visiting the mass graves of those who died and protesting against those who carried out the attacks," Patriotic Union of Kurdistan spokesman, Fatih Mohammed said.

Iraq launched gas attacks on Halabja and other towns in northern Iraq in 1988 as a reprisal against local Kurds who helped Iran during the Iran-Iraq war. More than 5,000 are thought to have died in the attack on Halabja.

KDP radio said on Saturday local television and radio stations would halt broadcasts for five minutes at 1200 local time (0900 GMT) and all places of recreation would be closed for the day. The KDP broadcast was monitored by Turkey's state-run Anatolian news agency.
